title: Optimize: eval safety & rollout playbook for prompt sets, regressions, A/B and rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams using Redwood Optimize need a deterministic, auditable, and automated way to decide whether a change (model/quantization/prompt-config/batching) can be promoted to production. Current ad-hoc checks cause delays and occasional regressions. This ticket defines the playbook: how we pick prompt sets, compute regression thresholds, run A/Bs, and trigger rollbacks.

Goals: (1) Define canonical prompt sets for major workload classes (chat, instruction, summarization, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings regression). (2) Specify numeric regression thresholds and confidence levels for automated pass/fail gating. (3) Define A/B test criteria and minimum sample sizes for rollout. (4) Define monitoring windows, alerting, and precise rollback triggers (automated and manual). (5) Provide a repeatable QA checklist and runbook for PM/Eng/DS to follow.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the runtime gates in production code nor instrumenting model internals. It also does not replace domain-specific acceptance tests for enterprise customers with bespoke prompts.

Why now: Optimize usage is increasing with Dedicated customers using autoscaling and private customers requiring stricter quality guarantees. A clear, codified playbook will speed rollouts and reduce regressions.
success_metrics: Reduction in post-release quality regressions attributed to Optimize changes by 60% within 3 months
Time to promote a change from canary to full rollout reduced from median 4 days to <=48 hours
Automated gate pass rate documented and stable across three consecutive releases (no more than 10% variance)
scope: Create canonical prompt sets and tagging schema for core workload categories
Define evaluation metrics for each workload (task-specific and generic: ROUGE/BLEU where appropriate, and embedding-similarity / semantic similarity metrics, and human-labeled acceptability)
Set numeric regression thresholds, confidence/CI rules, and minimum sample sizes
Document A/B experiment criteria, statistical tests, and rollout staging
Define automated alerting + rollback rules and a manual runbook for edge cases
Produce QA test checklist and ownership matrix (PM/DS/Eng)
out_of_scope: Custom customer prompt acceptance criteria (handled via enterprise onboarding)
Long-term research into new automated metrics beyond current similarity/acceptability signals
prompt_curation_guidelines: Maintain 3 canonical prompt sets per workload category: canonical, adversarial, and edge-case
Canonical set (~200 prompts): representative high-frequency user intents derived from telemetry and anonymized production prompts
Adversarial set (~50 prompts): targeted prompts designed to surface hallucination, repetition, and incorrect facts
Edge-case set (~50 prompts): long-context, truncated-input, mixed-locale, and system-prompt variations
Each prompt must include metadata: workload_tag, source_bucket (telemetry/bench/handcrafted), expected_output_pattern (free-text or structured), and human_evaluation_guidelines
eval_metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metrics by workload: chat -> acceptability rate (human-label pass %), summarization -> ROUGE-L and factuality score, RAG -> answer correctness and grounding rate, embeddings -> cosine similarity to reference vectors
Regression threshold defaults: no metric may regress more than 3 percentage points absolute for acceptability-like metrics, or 5% relative for similarity metrics, unless mitigated and approved
Statistical significance: two-sided t-test or bootstrap CI with alpha=0.05; effect must be beyond 95% CI and meet minimum effect size where applicable
Minimum sample sizes: canonical pass: 200 prompts per variant for initial gating; A/B phases require >= 2,000 impressions per variant or power calculation showing >=80% power for expected effect size
False discovery control: when running multiple metrics, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.10 to avoid spurious failures
ab_test_criteria: Staging cadence: experiment -> canary (5% traffic) -> ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%)
Success criteria to progress from canary: no metric violates thresholds; user-visible latency and error rate within SLA (latency +20% allowed for canaries) and no P0 incidents
If one metric shows small improvement and another shows a marginal regression within thresholds, require PM sign-off to continue
Minimum duration per stage: 48 hours at canary and 24 hours per subsequent stage unless sample size targets hit earlier
Traffic segmentation: randomization by token or session id with consistent bucketing for a user during experiment lifespan
rollback_triggers: Immediate automatic rollback: any P0 user-facing error spike (>=3x baseline error rate sustained for 10 minutes) or increase in latency beyond 2x baseline for >10 minutes
Quality rollback (automated): if primary acceptability or correctness metric drops below threshold and the drop is statistically significant at alpha=0.05 and effect size > configured minimum
Manual rollback: on-call engineer or PM can trigger after incident review; document reason and runbook steps
Stale-detection rollback: if canary fails to reach minimum sample size within 72 hours and trend indicates regression, revert and investigate
Graceful fallback: configure automatic fallback to previously pinned model variant for affected customers/regions while investigating
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-release dashboard with top-level acceptability, correctness, latency, error rate, and traffic split by variant
Automated alerts: severity-based alerts to #optimize-rollouts and on-call when thresholds breached; include diffs and CI PDFs
Daily digest during rollout: automated summary email to stakeholders with passage status and sample failure cases (with redaction)
Sampling for human review: sample 50 failing prompts/day automatically queued to DS/QA for triage during rollout
acceptance_criteria: Canonical prompt sets created, reviewed by DS and PM, and stored in Optimize prompt repo with metadata tags
A public doc (playbook) describing numeric thresholds, statistical rules, A/B flow, and rollback triggers published and linked in release notes
Automated gating checklist that can be executed manually by QA and programmatically via the eval harness (pass/fail outputs)
Handbook entry and runbook added to Confluence with contact list and escalation path
At least one staged rollout executed against a non-production traffic mirror using the playbook and documented outcomes
qa_tests: Run eval harness across canonical/adversarial/edge prompt sets and verify metrics computed match expected schema
Simulate canary with mirrored traffic to verify sampling, bucketing, and metric computation pipelines
Introduce synthetic regressions in a test variant to validate that gating and rollback logic would have triggered
Human review of 200 sampled outputs across workloads to cross-check automated metrics versus human labels
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize prompt sets and thresholds; DS/PM sign-off
Week 1: run dry-run on production mirror; iterate thresholds if necessary
Week 2: canary rollout at 5% for >=48 hours and sample review
Week 3: ramp to 25% then 50% following success criteria; continue daily monitoring
Post-rollout (2 weeks): run a release review summarizing metrics, edge failures, and lessons learned
roles_and_ownership: PM (Aisha Patel): playbook owner, final sign-off on rollouts and exceptions
DS (data science lead): create canonical/adversarial prompt sets and run statistical analysis
ENG (Ethan Morales): implement eval harness hooks, ensure telemetry captures required fields
QA: run human-labeling sprints and produce sample review reports
SRE: monitor runtime SLAs and execute automatic rollback mechanics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: canonical prompt sets are biased to historical traffic -> Mitigation: ensure prompt sourcing includes recent telemetry and a monthly refresh process
Risk: metric mismatch between automated signal and human perception -> Mitigation: continuous calibration via periodic human audits
Risk: noisy metrics cause false positives -> Mitigation: enforce minimum sample sizes, FDR control, and conservative thresholds for initial rollouts
Risk: rollout automation bugs -> Mitigation: run mirrored dry-runs and add unit/integration tests for gating logic
